subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 14, 2026
body:
geocode-glib update conflict resolved on installed AcreetionOS systems — if you've been staring at a broken update in the repair branch, it's fixed now. Head to the changelog to see the full package notes.

Development

Darren's calamares-config commits landed with two installer-level changes worth knowing about. The boot gfxmode now prefers 1008p over native 4K, which keeps older hardware from choking on high-resolution frames during install. Disk encryption has been removed from the default install flow; you can still set it up after the fact if you want it, and Darren's commit message about that is honestly peak engineering understatement. On the CI side, natalie pushed Secret Detection and SAST scanning into the GitLab pipeline across the project repos and shipped an MCP stdio server in us-infra-hub — the build infrastructure keeps getting sharper.

Community

Linus dropped kernel prepatch 7.3-rc3 for testing, so if you're running the cutting edge on AcreetionOS, grab it and report anything that feels off. EuroPython 2026 videos from Kraków are now published online; worth a browse if you missed the conference in July. And for the AcreetionOS faithful: the docs site has deep dives on kernel pinning and installer customization if you want to dig into how these pieces fit together. The wiki is also up to date with the latest flash instructions.

Tip of the day

After today's update, verify that geocode-glib resolved cleanly by running `pacman -Q geocode-glib` and confirming you get a clean version string with no conflict flags. If you hit anything strange, check the AcreetionOS forums or swing by Discord — someone's always awake with a fix. Then download the latest ISO if you're setting up a fresh system.
